title: Pricing experimentation circuit-breakers and security-questionnaire gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define a lightweight, auditable approval workflow and automated circuit-breaker system for pricing or packaging experiments that touch enterprise contracts and security questionnaire (SQ) commitments. This ticket covers policy, telemetry signals, temporary pricebook mechanics, and rollout/rollback runbook. Motivation: recent experiments with bundled Dedicated+Support pilot exposed inconsistent approval flows and a delayed revocation when enterprise SQ commitments were referenced in sales pitches. We need a repeatable pattern so PMs can run short-term pricing experiments without creating legal/SQ exposure or surprise revenue adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: A documented approval flow for (a) low-risk experiments (<=20% discount, <=3 months) and (b) high-risk experiments (>20% discount or >3 months or mentions of SQ/legal commitments) with clear approvers (PM, Sales Lead, RevOps, Legal, Security),
A technical circuit-breaker proof-of-concept implemented in pricebook service that can disable an experiment namespace via API and revert pricing for active customers within SLA,
Telemetry dashboard that surfaces experiment-specific activation events, revenue delta estimates, active customer count, and SQ-references seen in contract templates,
Rollout and rollback runbook with steps, Slack alerting, GitHub PR checklist, and post-mortem template, and two tabletop test runs executed with documented outcomes.
comments: 2025-02-11 — Kickoff with Legal and Security. Legal highlighted clause variations that can be introduced by experiments; recommended SQ gate for any experiment that references confidentiality, data retention, or KMS/HSM language.
2025-02-18 — Engineering (Marco) scoped a lightweight toggle in pricebook-service that supports namespaced experiment keys and a forced-revert endpoint. Estimate: 3 dev days + 1 day for infra tests.
2025-02-24 — RevOps suggested adding a revenue exposure calc to the dashboard (gross ARR impact and one-time credits). Action: RevOps to provide calc template by 2025-03-01.

2025-02-28 — Design reviewed notification copy for sales reps and customer success on experiment activation. Minor copy edits requested to clarify "temporary" nature and expected expiry date behavior.
2025-03-03 — Security requested proof that experiment toggles are RBAC-protected and audit-logged. Ticket DEP-377 created for infra audit logs; linked below.
2025-03-05 — PM review: added acceptance criteria for tabletop tests and two-stage approval (PM + one secondary approver) for medium risk experiments.
decisions: Decision: Two-tier approval model — 'Light' experiments (auto-approve by PM + RevOps notification) and 'Gate' experiments require Legal+Security signoff. Rationale: keeps velocity for small product-led tests while protecting enterprise commitments.

Decision: Circuit-breaker will be implemented as a single API that accepts an experiment_key and revert_mode. Revert_mode supports: 'immediate' (force current customers to prior prices) and 'grace' (apply new prices to renewals only). Default = 'grace'.
Decision: All experiment activations must create an immutable experiment record (owner, start/end, labels, SQ-references) and emit events to the experiments-dashboard topic.
notes_for_reviewers: Legal: please confirm SQ gating keywords list (KMS, HSM, data locality, retention, confidentiality). Security: confirm RBAC/audit requirements for toggles. Engineering: review revert semantics for active billing cycles and note any DB migration concerns.
